title: pulse: `nova-pulse commit` — the harvest commit step in Go, a rule per table row (#2549)
body:
bin/harvest-priority's $commit_step is 5.8 KB of bash inside a single-quoted
string inside an `ssh <bench> bash -s`, run on every UP bench every pass. In
twelve hours it broke three times and stranded finished work silently each time:
an unmatched glob under the Macs' zsh login shell (24 DONE cells never
committed, no log line); a `case ... DONE\(*` that did not parse on the remote
bash (no bench committed for seven hours, nothing landed overnight, the canary
failed, one `syntax error: unexpected end of file` per bench per pass the only
trace); and the patch for that broke the file itself. There was no test.

This is that step in Go, split the way the cards split it: harvestcommit.go is
the DECISION, one pure function from a job-directory value to a plan, with no
os, no exec and no git; harvestcommiteffect.go is the EFFECT, which applies a
plan and never re-decides. cmd/nova-pulse/commit.go is the verb.

It is its OWN verb and not a first step of `harvest --bench`, because the two run
in different places: `commit` runs ON a bench over its own working trees, while
`harvest --bench` runs on the coordinator and reaches a bench only through the
shell seam and a fetched ref -- it never has the working tree this step stages,
commits and rebases.

The rules, one table row each: the DONE PREFIX (`DONE (both runs green)` is
DONE, `DONEish` is not -- the rule that cost seven hours); read cards; the
DRAFT-ONLY list, now from a FILE rather than nine prefixes inside a shell string;
no repo; no RESULT.md; the exfiltration fence of #2609 in both halves (a changed
path that leaves the tree or carries a credential's shape is refused with the
path AND the shape, and a staged file whose CONTENT matches a key shape is
refused the same way, index reset, neither printing a byte of what it matched);
one changed file over 1 MB, refused by name; the card's own files set aside in
the job directory, never committed and never deleted; `rowan/<label>` under the
same branch rule every push here is held against; the card's declared PATHS
staged and nothing else (A4, #2522), with no card a printed WARN rather than a
refusal; the card-added scratch dropped in a follow-up commit; the rebase onto
the target at its live tip, REBASE-CONFLICT printed and aborted on a clash.

Two facts from #2549's comments are fixed here. EVERY VERDICT IS PRINTED: the
bash's driver greps `^HARVEST (JOB|NO-COMMIT|REFUSED|BENCH)` and drops every
SKIP, so the log holds 0 SKIP lines against 12,784 REFUSED while each studio
pass reported skipped=96 -- roughly 96 verdicts per bench per pass in the bin.
And the RESULT.md lines are WRITTEN, not substituted: `sed
"s#^BRANCH[: ].*#...#"` changes nothing when the line is absent and exits 0, so
`BRANCH-LINE report-nova-tools-2537-r1 -> ...` was printed 94 times and never
once took.

Two silent narrowings of the bash are gone: it globbed `*card-*` over slot names
(a slot cut under another name was never looked at) and took `ls -d $d/jobs/* |
head -1` (a slot holding two jobs lost one). And `git status --porcelain -z`
replaces `| awk '{print $2}'`, which loses the tail of any path with a space.

Tests: TestCommitDecision is one row per rule; TestApplyCommitPlanFixtureJob is
the positive control (a fixture job goes in, a branch whose two-dot diff against
the base is EXACTLY the card's PATHS comes out) with negative controls beside it
for DONEish, 1.1 MB, a key file by path and by content, the scratch drop and the
set-aside, all against real git repositories under t.TempDir(). TestCommitVerb
drives the verb end to end.

This does NOT delete bin/harvest-priority's $commit_step: that is the deploy
step, and #2549's DONE WHEN closes when the bash is removed on a rehearsal.
